datasets.name: NCI Imaging Data Commons
datasets.area: neuro; chest; body; breast; nuclear medicine
datasets.pathology: Many cancer collections (TCGA, TCIA, CPTAC, NLST, LIDC, and others), harmonized to DICOM
datasets.size: Portal of public cancer imaging, described by NCI as over 100 TB
datasets.license: Mostly CC BY; a minority of files are CC-NC (each file is tagged)
datasets.how_to_access: Browse collections in the portal. No registration. Files are in Google and AWS public buckets. Filter or inspect the license tag on each file before a commercial project.
datasets.limitations: This is a portal, not one cohort. More than 95% of files are described as CC BY, which allows commercial reuse with attribution, but a subset is CC-NC. De-identification and face-reconstruction risk still apply to head imaging. Not a substitute for reading the license on the files you actually download.
datasets.citation: Yes. Cite IDC and the underlying collection.

datasets.name: OpenNeuro
datasets.pathology: Many brain MRI studies, including healthy controls and disease cohorts, in BIDS
datasets.size: Repository of public BIDS datasets (size is per dataset)
datasets.license: Per dataset, usually CC0 after a 36-month grace period (check source)
datasets.how_to_access: Search OpenNeuro and open a dataset. Public versions download without a data-use agreement. Read that dataset’s license, README, and version DOI. New uploads can sit in a grace period before they are public.
datasets.limitations: Almost all current releases are CC0, but the license is per dataset and older uploads varied. These are BIDS NIfTI, not clinical DICOM. Many datasets are small research cohorts. Facial features on structural MRI are supposed to be removed; still do not try to re-identify subjects.
datasets.citation: Yes. Cite the version DOI. A HowToAcknowledge field, when present, is the authors’ requested wording. CC0 itself does not legally require attribution.

datasets.name: UPENN-GBM
datasets.pathology: Newly diagnosed glioblastoma, with segmentations and clinical/genomic tables
datasets.size: 630 subjects; about 357 GB (DICOM, NIfTI, and histopathology slides)
datasets.how_to_access: Open the collection page and use the download control in the Data Access table (TCIA Data Retriever or Aspera, whichever that row names). A public Creative Commons row does not need an application. Read the Citations & Data Usage Policy tab before use.
datasets.limitations: Glioblastoma cohort, not healthy controls. NIfTI volumes are registered to an atlas and do not align with the DICOM by design. Histopathology is NDPI, not radiology. Skull-stripped NIfTI is a different object from the DICOM.
datasets.citation: Yes. Cite the collection DOI on the TCIA page and follow the TCIA Data Usage Policy.

datasets.name: ReMIND (preoperative MRI and intraoperative ultrasound)
datasets.pathology: Brain tumors treated with resection, including intraoperative ultrasound
datasets.how_to_access: Open the collection page and use the download control in the Data Access table (TCIA Data Retriever or Aspera, whichever that row names). A public Creative Commons row does not need an application. Read the Citations & Data Usage Policy tab before use.
datasets.limitations: One collection covers preoperative MRI, segmentations, and intraoperative ultrasound (the ReMIND intraop ultrasound set). It is a surgical brain-tumor cohort. Ultrasound is intraoperative, not a screening exam. Pair images with the clinical table using the IDs on the collection page.
datasets.citation: Yes. Cite the collection DOI on the TCIA page and follow the TCIA Data Usage Policy.

datasets.name: Burdenko-GBM-Progression
datasets.pathology: Glioblastoma radiotherapy planning and follow-up, with RTSTRUCT/RTDOSE/RTPLAN
datasets.license: NIH Controlled Data Access Policy (images); CC BY 4.0 (clinical and genomic CSV)
datasets.how_to_access: The images can reconstruct a face, so they are not an open download. Follow the NIH Controlled Data Access Policy link on the collection page. The clinical and genomic CSV is listed separately under CC BY 4.0.
datasets.limitations: Do not assume the whole collection is CC BY. Only the small clinical/genomic table is CC BY 4.0. Imaging requires controlled access. Some MRIs are not in a canonical orientation. Registration between MRI and planning CT is not included; the submitters point to an external alignment container.
datasets.citation: Yes. Cite the collection DOI on the TCIA page and follow the TCIA Data Usage Policy. Imaging access is governed by the NIH policy, not only by CC BY.

datasets.name: Vestibular-Schwannoma-SEG
datasets.pathology: Vestibular schwannoma treated with Gamma Knife, with contours
datasets.how_to_access: Open the collection page and use the download control in the Data Access table (TCIA Data Retriever or Aspera, whichever that row names). A public Creative Commons row does not need an application. Read the Citations & Data Usage Policy tab before use.
datasets.limitations: Single-center radiosurgery cohort (contrast T1 and related RT structures), not a diagnostic screening set and not healthy controls. A separate multi-center set is Vestibular-Schwannoma-MC-RC.
datasets.citation: Yes. Cite the collection DOI on the TCIA page and follow the TCIA Data Usage Policy.

datasets.name: Vestibular-Schwannoma-MC-RC
datasets.pathology: Sporadic vestibular schwannoma, longitudinal MRI from multiple UK sites
datasets.how_to_access: Open the collection page and use the download control in the Data Access table (TCIA Data Retriever or Aspera, whichever that row names). A public Creative Commons row does not need an application. Read the Citations & Data Usage Policy tab before use.
datasets.limitations: Disease cohort only. Not every time point has both T1 and T2. This is a different collection from Vestibular-Schwannoma-SEG.
datasets.citation: Yes. Cite the collection DOI on the TCIA page and follow the TCIA Data Usage Policy.

datasets.name: LIDC-IDRI
datasets.pathology: Lung nodules marked by four readers; includes nodules that were not cancer
datasets.how_to_access: Open the collection page and use the download control in the Data Access table (TCIA Data Retriever or Aspera, whichever that row names). A public Creative Commons row does not need an application. Read the Citations & Data Usage Policy tab before use.
datasets.limitations: Thoracic CT with nodule marks, plus some chest radiographs. It includes scans without lung cancer, but it is not a healthy-volunteer set. XML annotations are part of the collection. Later DICOM-SEG conversions exist as separate TCIA collections.
datasets.citation: Yes. Cite the collection DOI on the TCIA page and follow the TCIA Data Usage Policy.

datasets.name: NLST (TCIA imaging subset)
datasets.pathology: Lung-cancer screening low-dose CT, mostly without cancer, plus cancer cases
datasets.how_to_access: Open the collection page and use the download control in the Data Access table (TCIA Data Retriever or Aspera, whichever that row names). A public Creative Commons row does not need an application. Read the Citations & Data Usage Policy tab before use. The full NLST clinical dataset is still requested through the Cancer Data Access System (CDAS). TCIA hosts the CT images and a public subset of the clinical data.
datasets.limitations: The TCIA copy is the public imaging release and a limited clinical subset, not every NLST variable. Screening CTs are low-dose and include a large majority of examinations without cancer. Histopathology slides are a separate download. Cite NLST as well as TCIA.
datasets.citation: Yes. Cite the collection DOI on the TCIA page and follow the TCIA Data Usage Policy. Also cite the NLST trial when you use the cohort.

datasets.name: Pancreas-CT
datasets.pathology: Healthy / non-cancer abdominal CT with pancreas segmentations
datasets.how_to_access: Open the collection page and use the download control in the Data Access table (TCIA Data Retriever or Aspera, whichever that row names). A public Creative Commons row does not need an application. Read the Citations & Data Usage Policy tab before use.
datasets.limitations: Normal pancreas anatomy for segmentation, not a tumor set. Confirm whether the label files you need are DICOM or an accompanying analysis format on the current download.
datasets.citation: Yes. Cite the collection DOI on the TCIA page and follow the TCIA Data Usage Policy.

datasets.name: CT Colonography
datasets.pathology: CT colonography with and without colorectal neoplasia
datasets.license: CC BY 3.0 and CC BY 4.0 (see the file table)
datasets.how_to_access: Open the collection page and use the download control in the Data Access table (TCIA Data Retriever or Aspera, whichever that row names). A public Creative Commons row does not need an application. Read the Citations & Data Usage Policy tab before use.
datasets.limitations: The collection mixes CC BY 3.0 and CC BY 4.0 files. Both allow commercial use with attribution, but credit the version you used. Includes non-cancer examinations. Prone/supine series and stool tagging vary.
datasets.citation: Yes. Cite the collection DOI on the TCIA page and follow the TCIA Data Usage Policy.

datasets.name: C4KC-KiTS
datasets.pathology: Kidney tumors (KiTS) with segmentations
datasets.how_to_access: Open the collection page and use the download control in the Data Access table (TCIA Data Retriever or Aspera, whichever that row names). A public Creative Commons row does not need an application. Read the Citations & Data Usage Policy tab before use.
datasets.limitations: Nephron-sparing and radical nephrectomy cohort from the KiTS challenge lineage, not healthy kidneys. Segmentations are included; confirm the SEG objects on download. Later KiTS challenges are not this exact TCIA release.
datasets.citation: Yes. Cite the collection DOI on the TCIA page and follow the TCIA Data Usage Policy.

datasets.name: CT-ORG
datasets.pathology: CT with liver lesions and metastases, labeled for lung, bone, liver, kidney, and bladder
datasets.how_to_access: Open the collection page and use the download control in the Data Access table (TCIA Data Retriever or Aspera, whichever that row names). A public Creative Commons row does not need an application. Read the Citations & Data Usage Policy tab before use. Download uses the Aspera plugin named on the page. Images are NIfTI, not DICOM.
datasets.limitations: Organ-segmentation set, not a pediatric set (see Pediatric-CT-SEG for pediatric chest/abdomen/pelvis contours). Many volumes come from LiTS and contain liver lesions. A few volumes are left-right flipped. Training labels for lung and bone were partly automatic.
datasets.citation: Yes. Cite the collection DOI on the TCIA page and follow the TCIA Data Usage Policy.

datasets.name: Pediatric-CT-SEG
datasets.pathology: Routine pediatric chest-abdomen-pelvis or abdomen-pelvis CT with expert organ contours
datasets.how_to_access: Open the collection page and use the download control in the Data Access table (TCIA Data Retriever or Aspera, whichever that row names). A public Creative Commons row does not need an application. Read the Citations & Data Usage Policy tab before use.
datasets.limitations: Ages range from 5 days to 16 years. Indications are routine clinical care, so some exams have disease and some do not; labels are organ contours, not diagnoses. Up to 29 structures, but structures outside the scan range are missing. Some series were reformatted to 2 mm and can have edge artifacts. Version 2 corrected skin contours.
datasets.citation: Yes. Cite the collection DOI on the TCIA page and follow the TCIA Data Usage Policy.

datasets.name: Pedi-Cranial-CT-Healthy
datasets.pathology: Healthy pediatric cranial CT (normative)
datasets.how_to_access: Open the collection page and use the download control in the Data Access table (TCIA Data Retriever or Aspera, whichever that row names). A public Creative Commons row does not need an application. Read the Citations & Data Usage Policy tab before use. The image package is MetaImage (MHA), not DICOM, and uses the Aspera download named on the page.
datasets.limitations: Explicitly healthy controls, ages about one month to ten years. Not DICOM. No lesion masks. Demographics are in a TSV. Useful as a normal reference, not as a hemorrhage or fracture dataset.
datasets.citation: Yes. Cite the collection DOI on the TCIA page and follow the TCIA Data Usage Policy.

datasets.name: Colorectal-Liver-Metastases
datasets.pathology: Colorectal liver metastases with segmentations
datasets.how_to_access: Open the collection page and use the download control in the Data Access table (TCIA Data Retriever or Aspera, whichever that row names). A public Creative Commons row does not need an application. Read the Citations & Data Usage Policy tab before use.
datasets.limitations: Preoperative CT in patients with colorectal liver metastases. Not a general abdominal CT set and not healthy liver.
datasets.citation: Yes. Cite the collection DOI on the TCIA page and follow the TCIA Data Usage Policy.

datasets.name: Soft-tissue-Sarcoma
datasets.pathology: Extremity soft-tissue sarcoma with FDG-PET/CT and MRI
datasets.how_to_access: Open the collection page and use the download control in the Data Access table (TCIA Data Retriever or Aspera, whichever that row names). A public Creative Commons row does not need an application. Read the Citations & Data Usage Policy tab before use.
datasets.limitations: Small limb-sarcoma cohort. Modalities are not complete for every subject. Different collection from QIN-SARCOMA.
datasets.citation: Yes. Cite the collection DOI on the TCIA page and follow the TCIA Data Usage Policy.

datasets.name: Spine-Mets-CT-SEG
datasets.pathology: Spinal metastases with vertebral and lesion segmentations
datasets.how_to_access: Open the collection page and use the download control in the Data Access table (TCIA Data Retriever or Aspera, whichever that row names). A public Creative Commons row does not need an application. Read the Citations & Data Usage Policy tab before use.
datasets.limitations: Radiotherapy-planning CTs in metastatic spine disease. Multiple primary cancers. Not a fracture or degenerative-spine set, and not healthy spine.
datasets.citation: Yes. Cite the collection DOI on the TCIA page and follow the TCIA Data Usage Policy.

datasets.name: QIN-SARCOMA
datasets.pathology: Soft-tissue sarcoma DCE-MRI, before and during preoperative chemoradiation
datasets.how_to_access: Open the collection page and use the download control in the Data Access table (TCIA Data Retriever or Aspera, whichever that row names). A public Creative Commons row does not need an application. Read the Citations & Data Usage Policy tab before use.
datasets.limitations: Formerly limited-access. The collection page says that as of April 2026, after discussion with the PI, it is public under CC BY 4.0. DCE-MRI only, three time points, and not every patient completed all visits. Acknowledge NIH award U01 CA154602 as the page requests. Not the same files as Soft-tissue-Sarcoma.
datasets.citation: Yes. Cite the collection DOI on the TCIA page and follow the TCIA Data Usage Policy. Also acknowledge U01 CA154602.

datasets.name: CBIS-DDSM
datasets.pathology: Curated mammography masses and calcifications, benign and malignant
datasets.how_to_access: Open the collection page and use the download control in the Data Access table (TCIA Data Retriever or Aspera, whichever that row names). A public Creative Commons row does not need an application. Read the Citations & Data Usage Policy tab before use.
datasets.limitations: A curated, decompressed subset of DDSM with updated ROIs, not a modern screening archive and not digital breast tomosynthesis. Includes benign (non-cancer) cases. Pathology labels are not a full clinical report.
datasets.citation: Yes. Cite the collection DOI on the TCIA page and follow the TCIA Data Usage Policy.

datasets.name: CMMD
datasets.pathology: Chinese mammography dataset with benign and malignant cases and molecular subtypes
datasets.how_to_access: Open the collection page and use the download control in the Data Access table (TCIA Data Retriever or Aspera, whichever that row names). A public Creative Commons row does not need an application. Read the Citations & Data Usage Policy tab before use.
datasets.limitations: Clinical mammograms from China, including benign and malignant disease rather than a pure normal-screening sample. Molecular subtype is not present for every case. Check the clinical table for which labels you can actually use.
datasets.citation: Yes. Cite the collection DOI on the TCIA page and follow the TCIA Data Usage Policy.

datasets.name: Duke-Breast-Cancer-MRI
datasets.pathology: Invasive breast cancer MRI with segmentations, radiomics, and outcomes
datasets.how_to_access: Open the collection page and use the download control in the Data Access table (TCIA Data Retriever or Aspera, whichever that row names). A public Creative Commons row does not need an application. Read the Citations & Data Usage Policy tab before use.
datasets.limitations: Non-commercial only. Invasive-cancer cohort, not screening normals. Some genomic fields are sparse. CC BY-NC is not the same as the CC BY used on many other TCIA collections.
datasets.citation: Yes. Cite the collection DOI on the TCIA page and follow the TCIA Data Usage Policy.

datasets.name: Breast-Cancer-Screening-DBT (BCS-DBT)
datasets.pathology: Screening digital breast tomosynthesis, with cancer cases and normal/benign exams
datasets.how_to_access: Open the collection page and use the download control in the Data Access table (TCIA Data Retriever or Aspera, whichever that row names). A public Creative Commons row does not need an application. Read the Citations & Data Usage Policy tab before use.
datasets.limitations: Non-commercial only. Large screening tomosynthesis set, so most exams are not cancer. Boxes and labels are not a substitute for the full radiology report. Files are large.
datasets.citation: Yes. Cite the collection DOI on the TCIA page and follow the TCIA Data Usage Policy.

datasets.name: FDG-PET-CT-Lesions (autoPET)
datasets.pathology: Whole-body FDG-PET/CT in lymphoma, melanoma, and NSCLC, plus studies with no PET-positive malignancy
datasets.size: 900 subjects; 1,014 studies. Defaced DICOM about 419 GB. Original images are a separate controlled download.
datasets.license: CC BY 4.0 (defaced images and clinical CSV); NIH Controlled Data Access Policy (original images)
datasets.how_to_access: Download the defaced DICOM and the clinical CSV from the collection page; those rows are CC BY 4.0 and do not need an application. Original images that include the head are under the NIH Controlled Data Access Policy linked on the page. The autoPET challenge site is a separate entry point and may not be this exact file release.
datasets.limitations: The openly downloadable images are defaced (head blacked out from the skull base up). If you need the face-containing originals, that is controlled access, not CC BY. Negative controls mean no PET-positive malignant lesion, not healthy volunteers. Manual tumor masks are on the PET-positive studies.
datasets.citation: Yes. Cite the collection DOI on the TCIA page and follow the TCIA Data Usage Policy.

datasets.name: PSMA-PET-CT-Lesions
datasets.pathology: PSMA PET/CT in prostate cancer with lesion segmentations
datasets.how_to_access: Open the collection page and use the download control in the Data Access table (TCIA Data Retriever or Aspera, whichever that row names). A public Creative Commons row does not need an application. Read the Citations & Data Usage Policy tab before use.
datasets.limitations: Prostate-cancer cohort. Confirm on the clinical table whether any studies have no PSMA-avid lesion before you treat them as negatives. Not FDG-PET-CT-Lesions.
datasets.citation: Yes. Cite the collection DOI on the TCIA page and follow the TCIA Data Usage Policy.

datasets.name: Prostate-MRI-US-Biopsy
datasets.pathology: Prostate MRI and ultrasound fusion biopsy, including benign biopsy results
datasets.how_to_access: Open the collection page and use the download control in the Data Access table (TCIA Data Retriever or Aspera, whichever that row names). A public Creative Commons row does not need an application. Read the Citations & Data Usage Policy tab before use.
datasets.limitations: Men referred for prostate biopsy, so the set includes cancers and benign histology, not asymptomatic screening normals. Ultrasound is targeted biopsy imaging, not a general ultrasound atlas. STL and segmentation side files may accompany DICOM.
datasets.citation: Yes. Cite the collection DOI on the TCIA page and follow the TCIA Data Usage Policy.

datasets.name: B-mode-and-CEUS-Liver
datasets.pathology: Focal liver lesions on B-mode and contrast-enhanced ultrasound
datasets.how_to_access: Open the collection page and use the download control in the Data Access table (TCIA Data Retriever or Aspera, whichever that row names). A public Creative Commons row does not need an application. Read the Citations & Data Usage Policy tab before use.
datasets.limitations: Liver-lesion cohort (the TCIA diagnosis list is liver cancer). It is not a normal-liver screening set. CEUS clips and B-mode stills are different series. Confirm which diagnoses are malignant versus benign in the clinical table.
datasets.citation: Yes. Cite the collection DOI on the TCIA page and follow the TCIA Data Usage Policy.

datasets.name: MIDRC-RICORD (1A, 1B, 1C)
datasets.pathology: COVID-19 chest CT and radiography, with non-COVID controls in 1B and 1C
datasets.size: 1A: 110 CT subjects. 1B: 117 CT subjects. 1C: 361 chest radiograph subjects.
datasets.how_to_access: Start at the 1A page, then download 1B (https://www.cancerimagingarchive.net/collection/midrc-ricord-1b/) and 1C (https://www.cancerimagingarchive.net/collection/midrc-ricord-1c/) the same way. Open the collection page and use the download control in the Data Access table (TCIA Data Retriever or Aspera, whichever that row names). A public Creative Commons row does not need an application. Read the Citations & Data Usage Policy tab before use.
datasets.limitations: Non-commercial only. 1A is COVID-19 chest CT. 1B adds CT controls. 1C is chest radiographs with COVID and non-COVID labels. These TCIA collections are the RICORD challenge sets, not the whole MIDRC portal. Pixel labels are not full reports.
datasets.citation: Yes. Cite the collection DOI on the TCIA page and follow the TCIA Data Usage Policy.

datasets.name: CPAISD
datasets.pathology: Hyperacute ischemic stroke on non-contrast head CT, with core and penumbra outlines
datasets.how_to_access: Open the Zenodo record and download the files. No account is required for the public files. The record names Kitware DicomAnonymizer as the de-identification tool.
datasets.limitations: Stroke cases only, single-center (City Hospital 40, Saint Petersburg). Core and penumbra contours are on slices where the readers marked them. Not a hemorrhage dataset and not a normal-CT dataset.
datasets.citation: Yes. Cite Umerenkov, Kudin, Peksheva, and Pavlov, CPAISD, Zenodo, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.10892316

datasets.name: CQ500
datasets.pathology: Non-contrast head CT with radiologist reads for critical findings (hemorrhage, fracture, and others)
datasets.size: 491 studies (Qure.ai release, redistributed on Academic Torrents)
datasets.how_to_access: Install a BitTorrent client and open the Academic Torrents page for hash 47e9d8aab761e75fd0a81982fa62bddf3a173831. The original headctstudy.qure.ai host is archived; confirm the license text on the torrent page and the archive of the Qure dataset page.
datasets.limitations: Non-commercial and share-alike. Reads are image-level labels, not full narrative reports. The original download site has gone offline, so this torrent is the practical public copy. De-identification was done by the releasing group; do not try to re-identify anyone.
datasets.citation: Yes. Cite Chilamkurthy et al., Deep learning algorithms for detection of critical findings in head CT scans, The Lancet 2018, and the CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 license.

datasets.name: RSNA Intracranial Hemorrhage Detection
datasets.pathology: Acute intracranial hemorrhage subtypes on head CT, including exams without hemorrhage
datasets.size: Over 25,000 head CT exams (RSNA description of the 2019 challenge)
datasets.how_to_access: Create a free Kaggle account, open this competition, accept the rules, then download from the Data tab. Do not pass the files to anyone who has not accepted the rules.
datasets.limitations: The rules page states non-commercial use only, and forbids redistribution and re-identification. Labels are slice- and exam-level hemorrhage subtypes, not segmentations and not reports. An RSNA terms PDF and the RSNA AI-Challenge-Data description repeat the non-commercial limit and ask for a specific citation if you share results.
datasets.citation: Yes. Flanders et al., Construction of a Machine Learning Dataset through Collaboration: The RSNA 2019 Brain CT Hemorrhage Challenge. Radiology: Artificial Intelligence. https://doi.org/10.1148/ryai.2020190211

datasets.name: RSNA-MICCAI Brain Tumor Radiogenomic Classification
datasets.pathology: Glioma MRI labeled for MGMT promoter methylation
datasets.size: See the competition Data tab (glioma MRI volumes)
datasets.how_to_access: Create a free Kaggle account, open this competition, accept the rules, then download from the Data tab. Do not pass the files to anyone who has not accepted the rules.
datasets.limitations: Competition Data may be used only for the competition, academic research, and education. Commercial use and redistribution are prohibited. These competitions use Kaggle’s standard rules template; re-read this competition’s rules page before you rely on it. Post-challenge copies sometimes add a separate citation line. Glioma patients only. The task is a radiogenomic label, not tumor segmentation.
datasets.citation: Yes. Cite the RSNA-MICCAI brain tumor competition and its dataset paper. Check the rules page for the requested wording.

Fracture labels are not a full radiology report.

Cases are graded for degenerative disease. This is not a healthy-volunteer MRI set.

Study-level PE labels and some image-quality flags. Not full reports. A different, larger PE cohort with reports is INSPECT, under a Stanford agreement.

datasets.pathology: Intracranial aneurysms on brain CT, including studies without an aneurysm

An AWS Open Data copy is documented at https://registry.opendata.aws/rsna-intracranial-aneurysm-detection-dataset/ and is also non-commercial.
datasets.limitations: Kaggle rules: non-commercial, no redistribution to people who have not agreed. The AWS registry text (checked 2026-10-18) allows non-commercial academic and educational use, forbids re-identification, and requires a citation; one version of that text also restricts redistribution. Read the copy you actually download. About 200 studies have AI segmentations. The AWS description calls these CT brain scans.
datasets.citation: Yes. Cite the Radiological Society of North America Intracranial Aneurysm Detection (RSNA-ICA) Dataset, July 2025. https://doi.org/10.1148/dataset.ica.2025

datasets.name: SIIM-ACR Pneumothorax Segmentation
datasets.pathology: Pneumothorax on chest radiographs, with masks, including exams without pneumothorax
datasets.how_to_access: Create a free Kaggle account, open this competition, accept the rules, then download from the Data tab. Do not pass the files to anyone who has not accepted the rules.
datasets.limitations: A Kaggle DICOM chest-radiograph set with pixel masks. It is a competition download, not a CC0 dump. Competition Data may be used only for the competition, academic research, and education. Commercial use and redistribution are prohibited. These competitions use Kaggle’s standard rules template; re-read this competition’s rules page before you rely on it. Post-challenge copies sometimes add a separate citation line.
datasets.citation: Yes. Cite the SIIM-ACR pneumothorax segmentation challenge. Check the rules page for the requested wording.

datasets.name: MIDRC
datasets.pathology: Medical imaging, especially chest and COVID-era collections, with clinical data and reports where contributors included them
datasets.size: Portal; size depends on the collections you select
datasets.license: University of Chicago data-use agreement (non-commercial research by default; a separate commercial agreement exists)
datasets.how_to_access: Register at data.midrc.org (InCommon or ORCID, as the login page offers) and accept the data-use agreement. The current text is linked from https://www.midrc.org/midrc-data-use-agreement and from the portal. Download only after the agreement is accepted.
datasets.limitations: The default academic agreement is personal, non-commercial research at a non-profit or government institution. It forbids redistributing the data, and it is not a Creative Commons license. A commercial agreement is a different document. Collections can include reports and clinical fields; do not treat every row as images alone. RICORD on TCIA is CC BY-NC and is not this portal.
datasets.citation: Yes. Acknowledge MIDRC in presentations and papers, using the wording on https://www.midrc.org/midrc-acknowledgements

datasets.name: VinDr-CXR
datasets.pathology: Adult chest radiographs with radiologist bounding boxes and image-level diagnoses, including no-finding exams
datasets.how_to_access: Create a PhysioNet account, complete CITI “Data or Specimens Only Research” training, and sign the Credentialed Health Data Use Agreement 1.5.0. Then download version 1.0.0 from the Files section.
datasets.limitations: Credentialed research use. You may not share the files or re-identify anyone. Labels are boxes and global findings from 17 radiologists, not full narrative reports. Training labels are three independent readers; the test set is a five-reader consensus.
datasets.citation: Yes. Cite the PhysioNet record and the VinDr-CXR paper named on that page. PhysioNet also asks you to contribute code with publications that use the data.

datasets.name: MIMIC-CXR
datasets.pathology: Emergency and inpatient chest radiographs with free-text reports, across many findings and no-finding studies
datasets.how_to_access: Create a PhysioNet account, complete CITI “Data or Specimens Only Research” training, and sign the Credentialed Health Data Use Agreement 1.5.0. Download the DICOM release (version 2.1.0), not only MIMIC-CXR-JPG, if you need DICOM.
datasets.limitations: Credentialed research use only. No sharing, no re-identification, and code from papers that use the data should be shared back. Reports are included and were de-identified (PHI replaced with ___). Images had burned-in text removed. This is a hospital population, so “normal” means no acute finding was described, not a healthy-volunteer study. JPEG derivatives are a different PhysioNet project.
datasets.citation: Yes. Johnson et al., MIMIC-CXR Database (version 2.1.0), PhysioNet. https://doi.org/10.13026/4jqj-jw95

datasets.name: CT-ICH
datasets.pathology: Traumatic brain injury head CT with hemorrhage masks and slice labels; some scans have no hemorrhage
datasets.size: 75 public NIfTI subjects (82 collected; subjects 59–65 are missing from the image folder)
datasets.how_to_access: Create a PhysioNet account and sign the Restricted Health Data Use Agreement 1.5.0 on the project (current version 1.3.1). Research use only. An older 1.2.0 release was CC BY 4.0; do not assume that still applies.
datasets.limitations: The current release is not DICOM and is not the old CC BY package. Scans were saved from windowed AVI files into NIfTI, so Hounsfield units are not preserved. Faces were blurred. All subjects had traumatic brain injury; 36 of 82 had hemorrhage. Two radiologists marked hemorrhage type, fracture, and outlines.
datasets.citation: Yes. Cite the PhysioNet CT-ICH record (Hssayeni et al.) for the version you download.

datasets.name: COCA

datasets.size: About 29 GB on the AIMI listing (gated coronary CT plus non-gated chest CT)
datasets.license: Stanford AIMI research use agreement (non-commercial; commercial license sold separately)
datasets.how_to_access: Sign in on Redivis, open this dataset, and apply for access. Accept the Stanford research-use terms for this dataset (each dataset is a separate request). Non-commercial research is free. Commercial use needs a separate AIMI license: https://aimi.stanford.edu/datasets-commercial-use
datasets.limitations: Free access is for non-commercial research under a data-use agreement. Do not redistribute the files or the download link. Do not attempt to re-identify anyone. A paid commercial license is a different contract; check the current fee and terms on the AIMI commercial-use page. Two subsets: gated coronary CT with calcium segmentations and scores, and non-gated chest CT with scores. A calcium score of zero is not a full normal chest CT.
datasets.citation: Yes. DOI 10.71718/ge5g-ds80, as printed on the AIMI COCA page.

datasets.license: Stanford AIMI research use agreement (non-commercial; commercial license sold separately)

About half the patients had COVID-19 pneumonia, and about two-thirds of clips were read as having no abnormality. Frames were extracted and resized, so this is not a DICOM ultrasound export. GitHub and Academic Torrents mirrors may not carry the same terms; use the Redivis agreement for the AIMI copy.
datasets.citation: Yes. Cite the dataset DOI or the citation block on the Redivis page, and name Stanford AIMI. The companion paper is Kumar et al., POCUS Journal 2026.

datasets.name: Sunnybrook Cardiac Data
datasets.pathology: Cine cardiac MRI: healthy, hypertrophy, heart failure with infarction, and heart failure without infarction
datasets.size: 45 cine-MRI cases, in five zip batches (hundreds of MB each)
datasets.how_to_access: Open the Cardiac Atlas page and download the DICOM zip batches, contours, and the patient CSV. The page states a public-domain license. IDs were remapped; use the CSV to match 2009 challenge IDs.
datasets.limitations: Small challenge set. Pathologies are mixed with healthy cases. Contours are the left ventricle from the 2009 short-axis segmentation challenge. CC0 does not require attribution, but the page asks you to cite Radau et al. if you publish.
datasets.citation: Requested, not required by CC0. Radau et al., Evaluation Framework for Algorithms Segmenting Short Axis Cardiac MRI. The MIDAS Journal. http://hdl.handle.net/10380/3070

datasets.name: IXI
datasets.pathology: Normal, healthy adult brain MRI (T1, T2, PD, MRA, diffusion)
datasets.size: Nearly 600 subjects; about 27 GB across T1, T2, PD, MRA, and DTI archives
datasets.how_to_access: Open the IXI page and download the NIfTI archives and the demographic spreadsheet. No account. The project text makes the data available under CC BY-SA 3.0 and asks you to acknowledge the IXI website.
datasets.limitations: Healthy volunteers only, three London hospitals, NIfTI rather than DICOM. Share-alike: if you redistribute an adaptation of the dataset, that adaptation stays under CC BY-SA 3.0. The license sentence is easy to miss on the short download page; re-read it before a commercial project.
datasets.citation: Yes. Acknowledge the IXI dataset, https://brain-development.org/ixi-dataset/ (EPSRC GR/S21533/02).

datasets.name: ISLES'24
datasets.pathology: Acute ischemic stroke with admission CT/CTA/CTP and follow-up MRI infarct masks
datasets.how_to_access: Open the Zenodo record (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.16970401) and download the archive. No account is required for the public files.
datasets.limitations: Non-commercial and share-alike. Training split of the ISLES 2024 challenge, not the hidden test set. Stroke only. NIfTI in BIDS, with clinical variables, not DICOM. Multimodal series are not a single CT.
datasets.citation: Yes. Cite Riedel et al., ISLES'24, Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.16970401

datasets.name: UCSF-PDGM
datasets.pathology: Preoperative diffuse glioma (WHO grade 2–4) on a standardized 3T protocol, with IDH and MGMT status, BraTS-style tumor segmentations, and diffusion and ASL perfusion
datasets.how_to_access: Open the collection page and use the download control in the Data Access table (TCIA Data Retriever or Aspera, whichever that row names). A public Creative Commons row does not need an application. Read the Citations & Data Usage Policy tab before use. The image download uses IBM Aspera Connect.
datasets.limitations: Glioma cohort, not healthy controls. TCIA states the original DICOM is not available: images are skull-stripped, co-registered to the FLAIR at 1 mm, and released as NIfTI. Six IDs turned out to be follow-up scans of other patients and were renamed in version 3. A metadata sheet maps cases to BraTS 2021 IDs, so check for overlap before combining with BraTS. Single center, single scanner vendor.
datasets.citation: Yes. Cite the collection DOI 10.7937/tcia.bdgf-8v37 and Calabrese et al., Radiology: Artificial Intelligence 2022, and follow the TCIA Data Usage Policy.

datasets.name: TotalSegmentator CT dataset
datasets.pathology: Routine clinical CT scans with segmentations of 117 anatomical structures (organs, bones, muscles, vessels); version 3 adds 291 pediatric CTs
datasets.how_to_access: Open the Zenodo record and download the zip. No account is needed. The record also links a faster Dropbox copy and a 102-subject subset for a quick look. Earlier versions (1,228 images) remain on Zenodo under their own DOIs.
datasets.limitations: Labels are anatomy, not disease, and the scans have no normal or abnormal label even though many pathologies are present. NIfTI, not DICOM. The segmentations were made with a model-assisted workflow, so they can carry systematic errors; version 3 fixed many label errors and vertebra mix-ups. The paper describes version 1.
datasets.citation: Yes. The record asks you to cite Wasserthal et al., TotalSegmentator, Radiology: Artificial Intelligence 2023, and the Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22688904.

datasets.name: Medical Segmentation Decathlon
datasets.pathology: Ten segmentation tasks: brain tumor, hippocampus, lung tumor, liver tumor, pancreas tumor, colon cancer, hepatic vessels, spleen, prostate, and left atrium
datasets.size: Ten tasks, from 30 to 750 volumes each; test labels are not released
datasets.how_to_access: Use the AWS Open Data page. The bucket s3://msd-for-monai can be listed and downloaded with the AWS CLI and --no-sign-request, so no AWS account is needed. MONAI also ships a loader for these tasks. Task descriptions are on medicaldecathlon.com.
datasets.limitations: Built for a 2018 segmentation challenge, so each task targets one structure or lesion and the cohorts are small for some tasks (left atrium has 30 volumes). Test-set labels are withheld. The brain tumor task is drawn from BraTS 2016–2017 and the lung task from TCIA, so check overlap before combining with those sources. Share-alike applies if you redistribute adapted data.
datasets.citation: Yes. Cite Simpson et al., A large annotated medical image dataset for the development and evaluation of segmentation algorithms (arXiv:1902.09063), and Antonelli et al., Nature Communications 2022.

datasets.name: NYU fastMRI
datasets.pathology: Raw k-space and reconstructed MRI from clinical knee, brain, prostate, and breast exams, built for accelerated MRI reconstruction research
datasets.size: Over 1,500 raw knee and 10,000 DICOM knee exams, 6,970 raw brain exams, 312 prostate and 300 breast exams
datasets.license: NYU fastMRI Dataset Sharing Agreement (internal research or education only)
datasets.how_to_access: Read the Dataset Sharing Agreement on the fastMRI page and submit the online application with your institutional affiliation and intended use. Approved users get a personal download link. Each sub-dataset has its own agreement.
datasets.limitations: Internal research or education only. No redistribution, no sharing of the download link, no selling or monetizing, and no attempt to re-identify anyone; the agreement also asks you to destroy copies when your work is done. Most data are raw k-space for reconstruction, not diagnostic labels. DICOM is described for the knee set only. Not for clinical use.
datasets.citation: Yes. The agreement requires citing “NYU fastMRI” and Knoll et al., Radiology: Artificial Intelligence 2020 (doi 10.1148/ryai.2020190007), plus arXiv:1811.08839.
